To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

flexible-field similarity searching of 3-D databases using the MEP as a similarity measure is possible and that the results are significantly better than those of searching with rigid-field MEP similarity measures.

the similarity between the molecular electrostatic potentials of flexible 3-dimensional molecules cannot be adequately calculated by using a graph-theoretical approach to MEP-based searching, and that the use of a genetic algorithm that is capable of searching flexible molecules can improve the results obtained from similarity searches of large files of flexible 2-D and 3-D molecules.

the similarity between the molecular electrostatic potentials of pairs of molecules is affected significantly by the flexibility of the molecules and that a genetic algorithm can be used to identify better alignments of flexible molecules than it can for rigid molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for searching 3-D chemical databases for molecules that are structurally similar to a given query molecule.
the development of new methods and algorithms for searching large files of 3-D structures.
the development of a new approach to flexible field-based searching in files of 3-D chemical structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of flexibility in MEP-based similarity searching is not a simple matter of using multiple conformers to represent torsional flexibility, but that a more complex approach to flexibility, such as that described in this paper, is required.
the use of flexibility can improve the quality of MEP-based similarity searching, provided that the search method is able to find the correct alignments.
the GA approach to flexible MEP-based searching is a viable method for similarity searching in files of flexible 1-D or 2-D chemical structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MEP-based similarity searching of flexible 3D databases is feasible, provided the flexibility of molecules is represented by a sufficient number of conformations and the MEPs of these conformations are compared with a flexible-field-based similarity measure.
the MEP similarity measures that have been developed for rigid 3-D structures are not sufficiently flexible to allow the calculation of good alignments between pairs of flexible molecules.
flexible MEP-based similarity searching is a viable alternative to searching with the more established approaches to 3-D similarity searching.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flexible-field searching of 3-D databases is feasible, and that the MEP is an appropriate measure of similarity for this task.
flexible field-based searching is a promising technique for searching large 3-D chemical structure databases.
the similarity between the MEPS of flexible molecules is more sensitive to the conformation of the molecules than is the similarity between the shapes of their electron density surfaces.
